title: Plugin host descriptor v1
description: What the host guarantees to a plugin, and what the plugin may not touch. This is the plugin-facing half of the frozen G1 protocol: the plugin' runtime descriptor is produced by a verified release and may narrow these guarantees, never widen them.

api.description: Host API major. A plugin requesting anything else is Incompatible, not silently downgraded.

reservedEnv.description: Environment variables the host owns and passes to managed processes. A plugin that redefines one of these would be able to redirect the host' instance root or inherit another instance' relay session, so the list must be explicit rather than empty.

onlyBusinessMethods.description: The bridge may only reach the plugin' own authorized backend. Any generic passthrough would make the declared effect matrix meaningless.

grantsAnyCapability.description: A bridge call can never itself widen a grant. Capability changes go through the management RPC and a lifecycle transaction.

limits.description: Defaults fixed by G1: 256 MiB package, 1 GiB extracted, 128 MiB per file, 20 000 files. The host may lower them per instance; the values here are ceilings a plugin can never raise.
